lost: No step to find every consumer of the key (configs, CI/CD, cron jobs, provider last-used timestamps) before rotation
No canary or staged rollout with checks for 401/403 errors and new-key usage at each stage

No handling of cached secrets and TTLs, or of stragglers such as serverless functions, long-running workers, batch jobs and partner integrations; uses a fixed 24-hour wait instead of the longest job cycle or cache TTL
No end-to-end smoke test of the new key before revocation
No step to disable the old key before deleting it, to watch error rates after revocation, or to re-enable the old key if errors appear
No warning to keep secret values out of tickets, chat and logs
No incident process if the old key may have been exposed

Does not state that the old key must be removed from config files; it says only to mark the secret version deprecated or destroyed. The fallback in Prerequisites and Step 2 is also inconsistent: it points to Step 2b for a 'dual-credential shim' but describes application-side dual-key acceptance, which does not help when the provider itself cannot hold two active keys
